verdict.rationale: Logseq stores data as local files and markets itself as 'privacy-first' with no requirement to use its cloud, and community members confirm they self-host sync via third-party tools like Syncthing instead of the vendor's paid Sync service. However there is no first-party documentation of an official self-hosted sync backend that the vendor supports — Logseq's own Sync is a paid, vendor-hosted (though encrypted) cloud service, and self-hosting requires external tools not part of the product. missing for 10: first-party docs on an officially supported self-hosted sync backend, explicit statement of pure offline/local-only operation guarantees, and independent verification that no telemetry/cloud dependency exists.
